_about: What a due process hearing officer can generally order, in the words the complaint prints under V. Proposed resolution. The person drafting chooses; `detail` is their own quantity or specification (never suggested by the skill), and each item's `sources` name what it rests on — the person's own statement of the relief sought (F4) and any readings. Two remedies a hearing officer generally cannot grant are listed as `outsideAuthority` and are not offered — they may be kept only if the person drafting insists, and the report says so. `other` prints exactly what was typed and nothing else. `counselOnly` marks a remedy that exists only on a represented filing: fees are awarded by a court to a prevailing parent under 20 U.S.C. § 1415(i)(3)(B), not by the hearing officer, so the complaint reserves the right rather than asking the officer for them, and a self-represented parent cannot recover them. `reservation` marks that item as printing after the lettered remedies as its own paragraph — a reservation is not a remedy the district can grant at the resolution session. `note` is general information shown when the item is offered.

options.filingLabel: A finding that the District denied Student a free appropriate public education
Compensatory services to make up what Student missed
options.detailAsk: How much is sought, of what, and when?

options.filingLabel: An independent educational evaluation at the District’s expense
Convening of an IEP team meeting within a stated period
options.detailAsk: Within how many days, and to decide what?

options.filingLabel: A change of classroom, school, or program
Specified services and supports going forward
Reimbursement for what the Parent arranged and paid for
options.detailAsk: What was paid for, and how much? For a private placement, when the Parent gave the District notice of it (34 C.F.R. § 300.148(d) can reduce reimbursement where notice was not given).
options.note: Reimbursement for a unilateral private placement turns in part on the notice the Parent gave beforehand (34 C.F.R. § 300.148(d)); if the notice is in the record, cite it.

options.filingLabel: Training for the staff who work with Student
options.note: Ordered in some jurisdictions; treated in others as relief beyond a hearing officer’s authority. Ask for it as training for the staff who work with Student, not as discipline.

options.filingLabel: Reversal of the suspension or removal, and correction of Student’s records to reflect it
options.note: Expungement of a disciplinary record is beyond a hearing officer’s authority in most states; the ask is the reversal, with the records corrected to reflect it.

options.filingLabel: Production of the education records and service logs
A determination that Student’s current educational placement, as the last agreed IEP describes it, is the placement to be maintained during these proceedings under 34 C.F.R. § 300.518
options.detailAsk: Which placement is the last agreed one?
options.note: Stay-put operates by law once a complaint is filed (34 C.F.R. § 300.518); the ask is a determination of which placement it is, where that is in dispute.

options.filingLabel: Reservation of the Parent’s right to seek reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs under 20 U.S.C. § 1415(i)(3)(B)
options.detailAsk: Leave blank for the standard sentence — “The Parent reserves the right to seek reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs under 20 U.S.C. § 1415(i)(3)(B).” — or give the wording you use.
The relief sought, in the pleading’s own words
What is sought, and on what basis?
What is sought, and about which member of staff?
